entities.name: Bernardo Bandini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bernardo Bandini Baroncelli, a Florentine merchant, is primarily remembered for his pivotal, albeit ultimately unsuccessful, role in the Pazzi conspiracy of 1478. This audacious plot aimed to overthrow the powerful Medici family, who had effectively governed the Republic of Florence for decades. Bandini's participation, driven by a complex mix of Pazzi family loyalty, political ambition, and opposition to Medici dominance, culminated in the assassination of Giuliano de' Medici, a direct challenge to the established political order of Renaissance Italy.

On April 26, 1478, during High Mass at Florence Cathedral, Bandini struck the fatal blow against Giuliano de' Medici, stabbing him nineteen times. His co-conspirator, Francesco de' Pazzi, also assaulted the dying Giuliano. Simultaneously, other conspirators targeted Lorenzo de' Medici, Giuliano's brother, who managed to escape with injuries. The immediate failure of the assassination attempt on Lorenzo, combined with the swift public backlash against the Pazzi and their allies, spelled doom for the conspirators. Bandini, a key perpetrator, managed to flee Florence in the ensuing chaos, embarking on an arduous journey across Italy and beyond.

Bandini's flight led him through the Ottoman Empire, where he sought refuge, but his notoriety made him a high-value target for Medici retribution. Lorenzo de' Medici, leveraging his extensive diplomatic network and financial resources, relentlessly pursued Bandini. He was eventually apprehended in Constantinople by agents of Sultan Mehmed II, who, in an act of diplomatic favor to Florence, extradited him. Returned to Florence, Bandini was publicly executed by hanging on December 29, 1479, almost two years after the conspiracy, a stark symbol of the Medici's unyielding power and their ability to reach across vast distances to punish their enemies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bernardo Bandini's central role in the Pazzi Conspiracy directly led to the assassination of Giuliano de' Medici and intensified the political consolidation of Lorenzo de' Medici's power, triggering a significant regional conflict known as the Pazzi War.
